The editing should build in intensity until the final sequence becomes an overwhelming collision of medieval war, supernatural terror and personal tragedy.

No narration or spoken dialogue is necessary.

ORIGINAL WORLD AND CHARACTER LOCK

The setting is a fictional dying continent where ancient kingdoms survive among the colossal fossilized remains of creatures that once ruled the oceans.

An expanding religious military empire conquers the continent using armies, massive siege engines and enormous ritual bells that can alter the physical world.

The protagonist is SAREN, a lean, battle-scarred former imperial war-scribe turned exile, in his late thirties. Weathered olive skin, short dark hair with a single premature gray streak, tired gray-green eyes, an old scar cutting across the bridge of his nose, and an exhausted, haunted expression.

A massive, ancient, charcoal-colored sword forged from the metal of a shattered ceremonial bell.

His victories gradually erase his identity.

THE TRAILER

BLACK.

An immense metallic object vibrates in darkness.

A thin crack travels across its surface.

The camera pulls backward.

It is an ancient BRONZE BELL.

Half buried in black sand.

Its broken surface is covered in forgotten inscriptions.

A pale human hand enters frame.

Fingers touch the crack.

The first musical impact.

HARD CUT.

EXTREME CLOSE-UP.

A weathered man's eye opens.

SAREN.

His face is covered in dust and dried blood.

A violent explosion illuminates his features.

He turns.

The camera rack-focuses past his face.

Behind him, an enormous ancient city is burning.

THE CITY OF VARN.

An impossible settlement built among the colossal fossilized ribs of a prehistoric sea creature.

Black stone towers rise between enormous white bones.

Suspended bridges connect crooked palaces.

The music accelerates.

CUT.

CUT.

CUT.

An enormous bronze bell somewhere above the battlefield begins shaking.

CUT.

CUT.

The machine tilts.

Soldiers scatter.

Sand cascades from its shoulders.

It lowers its head.

Imperial horses panic.

The creature charges through the army.

Armored bodies and wooden siege structures are thrown aside.

The camera runs at ground level between fleeing soldiers.

A deep metallic vibration.

Iva smiling beside a campfire.

FLASH.

Saren stands alone on an endless plain covered in shallow water.

A soldier.

A prisoner.

A stranger.

CUT.

CUT.

CUT.

CUT.

BLACK.

THE NAMELESS EDGE

Silence.

スケートパークで連続トリックを決め、大ジャンプ中にスケートボードがスノーボードへモーフィング。雪山へ着地して華麗なグラトリを連発。最後は雪山からジャンプし、スノーボードがホバーボードへモーフィング。空中で爆発的に加速し、遠くへ消えていく。

【映像全体の画風】
全編を、力強い墨の筆致と透明感のある水彩で描く。
人物、ボード、背景、雪煙、空気の流れまで同一の手描き表現で統一。

人物の輪郭は筆圧の変化がある墨線。
顔と手足は明瞭に描き、衣服の陰影は墨の濃淡と水彩の重なりで表現する。
細部まで描く部分と大胆に余白を残す部分を使い分け、動作のシルエットを鮮明に保つ。

背景は和紙の上に描かれた水彩画。
青空は淡い群青と浅葱色のにじみ。スケートパークは灰墨、青灰色、薄い黄土色。雪山は紙の白を生かし、薄藍と藤色の影を置く。
主人公とボードの差し色を全編で引き継ぐ。

高速動作の軌跡に、かすれた墨の残像を短く残す。
踏み切りには鋭い墨の飛沫、着地には放射状の筆致、旋回には流麗な曲線を使う。
水彩のにじみは背景と軌跡に限定し、顔、手足、板の接触関係を溶かさない。
和紙の質感は画面内で安定させ、ランダムな粒状ノイズやちらつきにしない。

【動作と速度の原則】
技の密度、滑走速度、身体運動の美しさを最優先。
技を決めるたびに止まらず、着地の圧縮と回転の慣性を次の技へ接続する。
肩、腰、膝、足首の連動を丁寧に描く。
画風が抽象的になっても、身体の重心、ボードの回転軸、接地位置は明確にする。

主人公の顔、髪、体格、衣装を全編で統一。
基本の進行方向は画面左から右。
カメラが移動しても、進行方向と位置関係をつなぐ。

【0.0〜2.6秒｜連続トリックで開始】
冒頭からスケートパークを高速滑走中。
地面すれすれのカメラが、前輪の斜め前から後退追走。

力強い一蹴りからオーリーで低い段差を越える。
着地直後にフロントサイド180。
スイッチスタンスのまま、スイッチ・ポップショービット。
板だけが水平に180度回転し、足裏で正確にキャッチする。

テールを弾く瞬間に小さな墨の飛沫。
車輪の軌跡は細いかすれ線となり、すぐに消える。
背景の水彩が横方向へ流れ、人物と板は鮮明。
カメラは足元から全身が見える斜め横へ移る。

【2.6〜5.6秒｜フリップからグラインド】
低いバンクでキックフリップ。
板が長軸まわりに一回転し、両足でキャッチ。

着地から即座にオーリーし、レッジへ50-50グラインド。
両トラックがレッジに掛かる接触を明確に描く。
接触点から細い墨の擦過線が後方へ走る。

終端でポップし、フロントサイド180アウト。
膝で着地を吸収し、そのまま次の障害物へ。
前景のレッジが画面を横切る瞬間にカットをつなぐ。

【5.6〜8.6秒｜レールから大ジャンプへ】
レールへ斜めに進入。
オーリーから板を90度ひねり、ボードスライド。
板の中央がレールに接触し、腕と肩でバランスを取る。

終端で板を進行方向へ戻して着地。
続く小さなバンクでトレフリップ。
板の水平360度回転と長軸方向のフリップを組み合わせ、両足でキャッチ。

板の軌道を短い墨の曲線で強調。
回転が読める瞬間のみ輪郭を鋭く描き、すぐ高速滑走へ戻る。

低い姿勢で大型クォーターパイプへ突進。
斜め後方の広角追走。
ランプの曲面を大胆な墨線で描き、迫ってくる遠近感を強調する。

【8.6〜10.3秒｜大ジャンプ】
クォーターパイプで膝を圧縮。
リップを抜ける瞬間に身体を伸ばし、高く大きく飛び出す。

カメラは下方から主人公を追い、急上昇。
パークの構造物が画面下へ抜けていく。
主人公は膝を抱え、片手で板の側面をグラブ。

ここから画面に映るのは、主人公、ボード、水彩の青空と薄い雲のみ。
地面、水平線、建物、山は映さない。
薄い雲を背景に、主人公の墨の輪郭が明瞭に浮かぶ。

【10.3〜12.0秒｜スケボーからスノボーへ】
全身と板が収まるローアングル。
カメラは斜め下から短い弧を描き、変形する板を見せる。

グラブしている同じ一枚のスケートボードが、約0.7秒で連続的にスノーボードへ変形。
デッキが前後へ伸び、幅が広がり、ノーズとテールが滑らかに反る。
車輪とトラックは墨が吸い込まれるように下面へ一体化し、滑らかな滑走面になる。
上面に二つのバインディングが形成され、靴を包み込んで固定。

板の輪郭が変化する動きに沿って、水彩の差し色が新しい形へ広がる。
元の板の配色と模様を受け継ぐ。
板全体を液体に崩さず、変形の途中も一枚の連続した物体として描く。

主人公の放物線運動は継続。
頂点から下降へ移り、グラブを離して着地姿勢を整える。
空中で停止しない。

【12.0〜13.7秒｜雪山への着地】
カメラが下降する主人公を追って下へティルト。
画面下から初めて雪面が現れる。

同じ進行方向と落下軌道のまま、圧雪された斜面へ着地。
板を斜面に合わせ、膝を深く曲げて衝撃を吸収。

接地から白い雪煙と薄藍の水彩飛沫が扇状に広がる。
雪煙は粒と筆のかすれで描き、主人公を長く隠さない。
低い追走から広角へ切り替え、水墨の山稜と白い大斜面を一気に見せる。

【13.7〜17.1秒｜高速グラトリ前半】
ノーズへ荷重し、テールを持ち上げるノーズプレス。
板をしならせたまま高速で滑る。

ノーズを支点にテールを振り、ノーズバター180。
肩の先行、腰の回転、板の追従を一続きに描く。

スイッチ・テールプレスへ接続。
板の反発で小さく跳び、スイッチ・オーリー180で通常スタンスへ戻る。

カメラは板のすぐ横を低く並走。
板のしなり、接雪点、浮いた端部をはっきり見せる。
雪上の軌跡が一筆書きのようにつながる。
直立する間を挟まず、荷重を連続して移す。

【17.1〜21.0秒｜回転技を畳みかける】
浅いカービングからノーズへ強く荷重。
板の反発を使ってノーリー360。
空中で一回転し、進行方向に合わせて着地。

着地の圧縮からテールバター180へ連結。
雪面に墨と薄藍の半円を残し、スイッチスタンスへ。

小さなうねりでスイッチ180。
着地後すぐ、左右のショートカービングを二回。
切り返すたびに鋭い雪煙と短い水彩の飛沫。

斜め前の後退追走、板の側面、短い俯瞰を組み合わせる。
俯瞰では連続したS字と回転の軌跡を見せる。
画面の切り替えで回転方向を反転させない。

【21.0〜24.0秒｜ノーリー540】
自然な小さなロールへ高速進入。
肩を予備回旋し、深く沈んでからノーリー540。

斜め下の側面追走で、踏み切りから一回転半まで全身を見せる。
身体をコンパクトにまとめ、回転終盤で開く。
軌道に沿って、かすれた墨の弧と淡い水彩の帯が短く残る。

スイッチスタンスで斜面へ正確に着地。
膝で衝撃を吸収し、滑走を継続。
着地直前から直後まで一つのカットで描く。

【24.0〜25.7秒｜カービングから再ジャンプ】
大きなカービングターンで、斜面の先にある自然な雪のリップへ進入。
主人公がカメラの近くを高速通過。
扇状の雪煙が手前を横切り、その奥でリップへ駆け上がる姿を見せる。

カメラは斜め後方から追い、踏み切りと同時に上昇。
板の反発を使って雪面を離れ、大きく前方へジャンプ。
今度は回転を加えず、板を安定させて空へ抜ける。
雪山が画面下へ抜け、再び主人公と空が中心の構図になる。

【25.7〜27.4秒｜スノボーからホバーボードへ】
空中の主人公を斜め下から捉える、全身の見える連続ショット。

同じ一枚のスノーボードがホバーボードへモーフィング。
板の中央部に厚みが生まれ、両端が流線形に整う。
側面の墨線が分かれ、薄い浮遊フィンとして展開。
下面に二つの推進部が形成される。
バインディングは足を支えたまま低い固定具へ変形する。

板の差し色が下面へ流れ込み、青緑と群青の水彩光になる。
光は筆で描いた細い線として発光し、白飛びさせない。
元の模様と色を残し、同じ板の進化として見せる。

変形完了と同時に落下が滑らかに抑えられる。
主人公は膝を曲げ、上体を低く倒し、腕を後方へ流して加速姿勢に入る。
ホバーボードの機首が遠方へ向く。

【27.4〜30.0秒｜急加速して消えるエンド】
推進部の水彩光が短く圧縮され、次の瞬間、後方へ鋭く伸びる。
ホバーボードが空中で爆発的に加速。

加速開始の数フレームだけ、人物と板の輪郭を進行方向へ伸ばすスミア作画。
髪と衣服が一斉に後ろへ引かれ、身体に加速の力が伝わる。
カメラは追走しようとするが追いつけず、主人公が急速に遠ざかる。

斜め後方からの構図で、主人公は画面右奥の空へ向かう。
最初は全身が見える大きさ、次に小さなシルエット、最後に一点へ。
遠近によって小さくなり、ついに視認できなくなる。

後方には一本の長い墨の軌跡と、青緑の水彩の帯が残る。
軌跡の根元が画面手前を鋭く横切り、奥へ細く収束する。
水彩の帯が空へゆっくりにじみ、墨のかすれがほどける。

最後の約0.4秒は、誰もいない広い水彩の空と、消えかけた一筋の軌跡。
急加速の風切り音だけが遠ざかって終わる。

【カメラ・編集】
地面すれすれの追走、側面並走、斜め前の後退撮影、短い俯瞰、ジャンプを追う上昇撮影を組み合わせる。
技の踏み切り、回転、キャッチ、着地が読める画角を選ぶ。
高速部分でも、板と足をフレーム外へ切り落とさない。

短い寄りカットと、全身の技を見せる追走カットでテンポを作る。
モーフィングはカットで省略せず、連続した形状変化を見せる。
水彩のにじみと墨の軌跡は動作を強調するために使い、動作そのものを隠さない。
長いスローモーションを入れず、最後の急加速まで勢いを積み上げる。

【音】
BGM、セリフ、ナレーションなし。
前半は車輪の走行音、テールを弾く乾いた音、レールの擦過音。
中盤は空中の風、雪の圧縮音、エッジが雪を切る音。
モーフィングには短い流動音と低い共鳴。
最後は推進部の低い立ち上がりから、鋭い加速音と遠ざかる風切り音。
技の接触と音のタイミングを正確に同期する。

【ネガティブ】
写実的3DCG、プラスチック質感、全編一様なぼかし、過剰なネオン。
技の削減、技順の変更、同じ技の反復、長い停止、長いスローモーション。
墨や水彩に埋もれて読めない身体、顔のにじみ、手足の増殖、衣装変更。
板の複製、足と板の接触破綻、変形途中の唐突な置換。
スケボーからスノボーへの変形中に映り込む地面や山。
フラッシュだけで場面を切り替える演出。
ホバーボードの車輪、消失時の単純な透明フェード、突然の瞬間移動。
白飛び、粒状ノイズ、文字、字幕、実在ブランドのロゴ。

prompt:
CLEAR
30-SECOND SINGLE CONTINUOUS SHOT: STRICT ONE-TAKE

PRIMARY DIRECTIVE
Create a 30-second uninterrupted shot on a busy Paris street in the 1950s.
ONE PHYSICAL CAMERA. ONE TAKE. ONE CRT TV CHARACTER.
No cuts, transitions, montage, time jumps, hidden cuts or camera switching.
The operator physically follows the same CRT character along one short route.
Camera height and framing may change only through continuous physical movement.
The film feels like a forgotten black-and-white French New Wave fantasy on an old
35mm reel: playful, melancholic, tactile, spontaneous, poetic and imperfect.

LOVART: PHYSICAL BRAND DETAILS
The dress shop is named LOVART. Its aged painted storefront fascia carries only
the exact uppercase word "LOVART", in simple period-appropriate lettering.
A small weathered paper poster beside the open dress display carries the same
word "LOVART" in large, high-contrast letters, positioned at the character's hand height.
Both are physical objects within the street, with natural perspective and texture.
The poster lettering starts smudged and becomes readable only along the hand wipe.
The untouched shop fascia stays smudged until the final global reveal.
Keep the spelling and prop locations consistent. No other advertising copy.
No floating branding, overlay logos, modern screens or added title cards.
Do not put the brand on the character's CRT screen.

CHARACTER AND PERFORMANCE
The protagonist is one adult human-bodied figure with a vintage CRT television
instead of a human head. Lean adult proportions, dark charcoal suit jacket,
white open-collar shirt, matching trousers and worn black leather shoes.
Natural human hands. The TV head has a dark-brown woodgrain rectangular casing,
a rounded convex glass screen, small side control knobs and two thin metal antennas.
The screen displays subdued monochrome analog static, with no human face or text.
Preserve this exact casing, screen, antennas, costume and body throughout the take.
Its head remains a physical television. Never reveal a human head inside it.
No clown makeup or circus outfit.
It is charming, vulnerable and absurdly theatrical, never frightening.
Express happiness through an upright torso, buoyant steps, open arms and an eager
head tilt. Express sadness through dropped shoulders, a lowered TV head, stillness
and hesitant hands. Preserve the CRT screen's subdued analog static; subtle analog
brightness and signal variations may support performance, confined to the screen.
Do not add human eyes, a mouth, an emoji face or a talking face to the display.
Body language carries the story. No dialogue is needed.

SURREAL SMUDGE MECHANIC
At the start, reality itself is partially erased. Individual people and objects
carry translucent, surface-bound smudging, as if rubbed out under frosted glass.
This is NOT lens blur, missed focus, a dirty lens, Gaussian blur or a global filter.
The camera works normally. The protagonist and its touching hand remain readable.

The CRT character removes smudging through DIRECT HAND CONTACT.
Its palm and fingers physically touch the actual subject surface.
Detail appears directly beneath and immediately behind the moving fingers,
following the exact contact path. First recognizable contours emerge, then texture,
then full natural detail. Untouched areas of the same subject remain erased.
Every revealed area STAYS REVEALED for the remainder of the take, including when
it leaves and re-enters view. No instant whole-object transformation.

No magical glow, particles, sparks, beams, waves, morphing or digital transition.
The effect feels like an impossible but tactile practical illusion.
Only the final lens contact creates the single global exception described below.

SPATIAL CONTINUITY
Arrange the pole, gentleman with dog, open shop display and elderly woman along
one compact route, only a few steps apart. The elderly woman waits beside a narrow
side-street crossing. Keep the full route walkable within 30 seconds.
Background pedestrians continue naturally. No one teleports or changes identity.
Use continuous reframing to keep hand contact visible during each wipe.

CONTINUOUS ACTION: TIMESTAMPED BEATS, NOT SEPARATE SHOTS

00–05 SECONDS: STREET POLE
Begin with a wide handheld view of the inhabited Paris street. People, buildings
and objects contain visibly smudged surfaces beside ordinary readable details.
The CRT character enters frame left, grabs a pole and swings around it with
childlike enthusiasm. Its costume reacts naturally to the turn.
It stops, turns its screen toward the camera and opens its arms triumphantly.
Then its shoulders collapse and its TV head droops in exaggerated sadness.
Hold one brief comic beat. It notices the dog a few steps ahead.

05–11 SECONDS: DOG
The operator follows as the character approaches a gentleman walking a dog.
The dog is initially a smudged silhouette with little visible fur detail.
The character crouches and gently wipes its flank with direct palm contact.
Fur and contours emerge only along the hand's path; untouched fur remains erased.
A second gentle pass across the cheek reveals the eye, nose, whiskers and hairs.
All revealed detail stays sharp. No whole-frame sharpening occurs.
Delighted, the character briefly crouches like the dog, tilts its TV head and
playfully imitates one paw movement. The gentleman reacts with confused amusement.
The character rises and moves to the adjacent shop. Keep this imitation brief.

11–18 SECONDS: DRESS
An elegant vintage dress hangs at the LOVART boutique's OPEN SHOP DISPLAY,
beside the window and within reach. It begins as a partially erased shape.
The character touches the actual fabric, not glass in front of it.
One deliberate pass reveals fabric folds, seams and embroidery along its contact path.
Untouched sections remain smudged. Its hand then wipes once across the reachable
paper poster beside the dress, progressively uncovering the word "LOVART" precisely
behind its fingers. The revealed lettering remains permanently readable.
Frame both the hand and letters clearly during this brief action.
The character performs one small aristocratic curtsy, keeping the beat compact.
Its TV head rises proudly, then suddenly sinks with theatrical heartbreak.
It notices the elderly woman waiting at the nearby crossing.

18–25 SECONDS: GRANDMOTHER

映像の総尺は厳密に15秒。以下の時間指定は完成映像上の再生時間。前シーンの直後から始まり、ファルカーメンの忠告、ギャングの攻撃、片手による制止と投擲、テーブルへの激突、別のギャングによる銃の威嚇、店内の人々の恐怖、動じないファルカーメンまでを描く。
劇場版クオリティのサイバーパンクアニメ。力強く整った人物作画、精密な背景、立体的なセル調の陰影。青緑とマゼンタのネオン、カウンターの琥珀色の照明が、黒い仮面、肌、酒瓶、グラスへ反射する。静かな会話から一瞬の激しい動きへ切り替わり、最後は張り詰めた静けさへ戻る。

参照画像の全身像と顔のアップは、同じ一人のキャラクターを示す資料として扱う。映像に登場するファルカーメンは一人だけ。資料の白背景、文字、分割構図は使用しない。

前シーンで仮面を殴って右手を痛めた男は、今回も右手を押さえたまま周囲に残る。今回殴りかかるのは、両手に負傷のない別のギャング。後半で銃を構える男も、投げ飛ばされる男とは別人とし、それぞれ髪型と衣装で明確に区別する。

ファルカーメンを胸から上のミディアムショットで捉える。手前にギャングたちの肩を配置し、取り囲まれていることを示す。

ファルカーメンは仮面をゆっくり左右へ向け、周囲を見回しながら、落ち着いた声で日本語の台詞を言う。

ファルカーメン：
「暴力はいけない。店に迷惑だ」
相手を諭すような、静かではっきりした口調。「暴力はいけない」の後に短く間を置き、「店に迷惑だ」と続ける。怒鳴らず、挑発する笑みも浮かべない。口元を日本語の発音に自然に同期させる。

声質は前の注文シーンと同じ、既出の音声ファイル1を参照したファルカーメンの声を維持する。

カメラがわずかに横へ移動し、忠告を聞いて眉をつり上げるギャングたちの表情を背景に見せる。

両手に負傷のないギャングが、顔を怒りでゆがめ、一歩踏み込む。周囲の仲間も苛立ち、前へ身を乗り出す。

攻撃するギャングが日本語で叫ぶ。

ギャング：

叫びの終わりに合わせて右拳を引き、そのままファルカーメンの顔へ向けてパンチを繰り出す。後ろのギャングたちは取り囲む位置を保ち、主となる攻防を隠さない。

Image 4 binds canned meat, a few peas, gravy, old metal trays, and spoons. Build three identical meals with the same plate style. Image 4 shows one serving only as material reference, not as the final table count.
All four images are asset boards only. The final result must be one continuous cinematic image space, excluding panel layouts, white background, labels, and duplicated character views.

[Space, Seats, and Axis]
Use the table itself for orientation. North side faces deeper into the room; south side faces outward.
Alin sits on the north side, west end, torso facing south.
Lisa sits on the west side, north end, torso facing east.
They sit at right angles across the northwest corner of the table, shoulders about half a meter apart, close enough for their near forearms to meet naturally.
The empty third chair is on the south side, slightly west, with the third meal directly in front of it on the south inner edge of the table.
Both women keep their hips on their own chairs, both feet on the floor, chair legs fixed, no standing, no seat changes. When Alin reaches out she only leans slightly forward, with restrained post-injury movement but no newly visible wounds.

The master camera side is outside the northwest corner looking southeast, so Alin stays screen left and Lisa screen right; the empty chair sits in the middle-to-background on the far side of the table. All human camera positions stay on the northwest outer half-plane of the Alin-Lisa axis and never cross it. In singles, Alin looks screen-right toward Lisa, Lisa looks screen-left toward Alin; when either looks to the empty chair, the eyeline must truly land on the south-side empty seat. Eyes find the target first, head follows in a small delayed movement. Height changes are allowed, but seat positions, table edges, and plate correspondences never change.

[Three Meals Locked from Frame One]
Frame one must already show three complete, neatly placed, matching meals at the same time:
A in front of Alin on the north side,
B in front of Lisa on the west side,
C in front of the empty south chair.
A/B/C are production labels only and never appear on screen.
All three are matching old metal trays from Image 4, each already holding the same type of meat chunks, near-matching size and count, the same amount of gravy, and a few peas. Portion size, plating height, and completion state match closely. None are empty plates. All food was prepared before the scene begins. There is no scooping, serving, topping off, passing plates, or bringing food in from off-screen during this clip.

The opening shot must use enough depth of field to show all three meals clearly and tie each one to its correct seat. Alin’s own plate must not be blocked by her body, forearm, kettle, or framing. These are three separate meals, not one meal shown three ways. A stays in front of Alin, B stays in front of Lisa, C stays in front of the empty chair. A and B never move. C is adjusted only once in shot 1 by about 1 cm and then stays fixed in the same empty-seat place. No one eats, so the food amount, proportions, and internal arrangement remain unchanged throughout. When plates go out of frame in close-ups, they still exist off-screen. Whenever the table is seen again, it must inherit the same three-plate state without regenerating the table layout.

[Tabletop and Hand Continuity]
All three meals stay clearly separated by visible wood gaps between plates. C is within Lisa’s natural left-hand reach, with no standing, no leaning across the table, and no exaggerated arm extension. The opened canned-meat tin stays on the east side of the table; the serving spoon already rests inside it with the handle leaning against the rim. No one touches the can or serving spoon. A kettle and cup also stay on the east side and never block the three plates. The food is room temperature and gives off no steam.

There are three personal spoons, one per plate, each placed to the right of its own tray with the bowl near the rim, all readable at the start. At the end Lisa grips the personal spoon beside B. Alin’s spoon and the empty-seat spoon never move. The serving spoon and personal spoons are never confused, duplicated, added, or removed.

Opening hand positions:
Alin’s right forearm rests on the table, palm down, to the right of her own plate near the northwest corner, without covering A. Her left hand rests empty on her left thigh and stays there throughout.
Lisa begins with both hands empty: her right hand rests beside B near her own spoon but does not hold it; her left fingertips lightly touch the near rim of the already-set C plate.
Lisa’s left hand performs only one small adjustment of about 1 cm, then releases the rim and withdraws along the tabletop toward the northwest corner.
Alin then places her right hand over the back of Lisa’s left hand and keeps it there until the end.
After contact, no palm-flip, no hand swap, no interlaced fingers; Lisa only relaxes slightly through her fingertips.
In shots where the hands are off-screen, these states still continue.
The only new end action is Lisa’s right hand moving to grip the personal spoon beside B, with the spoon bowl still resting at the plate edge. All food remains on its original plates.

[Performance Rules]
Before the clip begins, Lisa has already prepared all three meals and is trying to hold order together through the small act of straightening the third plate. “I made three portions again.” refers to the serving having already happened earlier; it must not trigger any new serving action. At the opening she is already tired and slightly red-eyed but not yet audibly crying. Her gaze moves from the food to the empty chair, then back to the third plate. She pauses. Moisture gathers at the lower eyelids. She tries to press her lips together and control her breath, but loses control midway through one inhale. The crying comes from chest and throat; lips part naturally for breathing; face shape stays intact; no wide-mouthed wailing or head-thrown-back sobbing. After the break, there are only two clearly visible shoulder/back jolts; the rest is small, irregular breath movement. After Alin touches her, Lisa does not stop crying instantly; she first registers the warmth on the back of her hand, then looks up to find Alin. By the end she has only earned one slightly longer exhale; tears and residual sobbing remain.

Alin’s objective is to bring Lisa back to the presence beside her and gently move her toward taking even one bite. She is also exhausted. Hearing Lisa cry, her jaw tightens briefly and her eyes moisten. She first adjusts one breath for herself, then chooses to reach out. Each close-up should carry one main change only: restraining breath, starting the reach, waiting for eye contact, softening the gaze. Keep subtle eye-target shifts and natural blinks, with reflections motivated by real lamp position, never glassy staring. She does not perform stoic slogans or fake smiles. Her hand stays quiet on Lisa’s hand. Their reactions are staggered: Lisa breaks first, Alin is affected second, Lisa is then influenced by Alin’s steadier breathing. No synchronized blinks, synchronized tears, or mechanical nodding.

[Voices and Dialogue]
Lisa, the short-haired leather-jacket woman from Image 2: adult female, natural mid-high register, soft with slight breathiness, clear natural English; crying gradually damages breath support but never stretches every syllable.
Alin, the long-haired white-top woman from Image 1: adult female, natural mid-low register, gentle English with chest support, quiet but clear; line endings tremble slightly when containing grief, and become softer in comfort, never lecture-like.
Voice identity, accent, and age stay stable across cuts. Only the designated speaker speaks in each line. Lisa’s soft nonverbal crying may continue under Alin’s dialogue but must not cover the words.

Use only these six lines, once each, at the assigned points:
Lisa: “Hia…”
Lisa: “I made three portions again.”
Alin: “I miss her too.”
Alin: “We need to stay strong.”
Alin: “Eat a little…”
Alin: “We still have to get out—together.”
The ellipsis and dash indicate short pauses only, not extra words. All dialogue is natural real-time speech. Pauses belong to breath and eye contact, not time-compressed dubbing.

[Look, Palette, and Light]
Grade the whole piece as realistic survival drama: low-saturation warm tungsten interior, gray-brown ruin materials, preserved skin tone, continuing the warm lamp and old textures from Image 3.
Palette direction only, never shown as text:
coal black #282624 for deep structure and shadow,
weathered wood brown-gray #665548 for table, chairs, and walls,
dark moss olive #555647 for sofa and background,
restrained amber #BA8C53 for lamp warmth and metal reflections,
old ivory #D9D0C1 for the lit planes of Alin’s white top.
Keep Lisa’s jacket orange-brown but reduce harsh saturation; keep natural blood in skin; blonde hair must not bleach to white.

The hanging lamp is the fixed world light source, around 3000–3200K tungsten. Overall white-balance direction is around 3800K so the lamp stays warm while faces do not turn orange. Walls and table provide weak natural bounce, preserving detail in the shadow side of eyes, mouth corners, and fingers. When camera angle changes, light direction changes according to real space only. Shadows stay neutral gray-brown, dense but never crushed. Highlights roll softly, preserving white-shirt wrinkles and forehead texture. Exposure, saturation, black level, and grain remain constant through the whole clip. After the comfort begins, the light must not become warmer, brighter, or emotionally “improved.” Keep a slight fine grain and a small halo around the lamp, without skin-smoothing or oversharpening; eyes and hands remain clear.

[Material Physics and Environment]
Everything obeys contact, gravity, and real material response. Lisa’s leather jacket forms brief elbow creases when she lifts her arm and naturally settles afterward; sobbing causes tiny delayed movement at shoulder seams and shearling collar; the leather keeps weight and thickness, and the waist cinch limits large torso bending. When Alin leans in, the white camisole compresses into waist folds, straps stay in place, and the jeans hold stable weight creases at the hips. Sleeves, forearms, and table edges create light friction and contact shadows. Clothes never clip through the table, never change design, and never respond to nonexistent indoor wind. Lisa’s short hair lags slightly when she lowers her head, then settles. Alin’s long hair moves softly with small head turns and never hides the eyes.

Tears first collect at the lower lids, then slide slowly down the real slope of the cheeks, leaving narrow irregular wet tracks. These tracks must persist across later shots; never reset to a dry face, never create floating droplets or glamour tear highlights. When Alin’s hand lands, it creates a slight skin compression and soft contact shadow. Finger count, joints, and wrist connections stay stable.
All meat is already on the three plates and stays stable. Only C produces a very shallow gravy ripple during the one slight adjustment, then settles. A and B remain still. No dropping, flying-in food, multiplication, or liquid changes.
Only a few floating dust particles exist in the room, briefly visible near the hanging lamp when caught by backlight, then disappearing into shadow. No new dust burst, no smoke layer, no face-covering haze. Dust belongs mainly to the establishing shot; face close-ups prioritize skin, eyes, and tear tracks.

[25-Second Seven-Shot Timeline]
00:00–00:04, Shot 1, 35mm feel, fixed medium-wide, high oblique about 45 degrees from the northwest side, with enough depth of field to cover the whole table.
The first frame must clearly show the complete A plate in front of Alin, the complete B plate in front of Lisa, and the complete C plate in front of the far empty chair, all three matching meals already plated and readable with no major blockage. Hold about one second so the viewer can read the relationship between two women and three meals. Then Lisa’s left fingertips nudge the already-set C plate about 1 cm. Her right hand stays empty beside B’s spoon. Her gaze rises from C to the empty chair. Her left hand freezes on the rim. Alin stays still in her opening pose, looking down at A. One short, quiet plate-on-wood sound only. Cut on the moment Lisa’s motion stops while her fingertips are still at the rim.

00:04–00:06, Shot 2, low close shot about 15 cm above the tabletop, looking toward the south-side empty chair.
Camera locked. Perform only one smooth rack focus: from the already-full C plate rim and Lisa’s fingertips into the empty chair back behind it. A and B still exist in place but are out of frame for this lens choice only. Lisa releases the rim and slides her left hand back along the tabletop to settle palm-down near the northwest corner. Her right hand remains empty beside her own plate. Hold one short beat on the empty chair in focus. Around 00:05.1–00:05.8, Lisa softly says off-screen, “Hia…,” as if still waiting for her to come take the meal. Let the tail fall into nothing. Room tone continues. Cut into Lisa’s eyes receiving the emptiness; do not repeat the call.

00:06–00:11.5, Shot 3, 85mm feel, Lisa eye-level three-quarter profile close-up, keeping jawline and shoulders.
For about the first three seconds, push in extremely slowly around 15 cm, then hold. Lisa’s eyes stay on the empty chair, then drop to the third meal. Moisture gathers at the lower eyelids. Around 00:06.3–00:08.7 she quietly says, “I made three portions again.” The first part tries to stay level; “again” lands gently. She presses her lips together afterward and tries to finish an inhale, but the breath breaks in the middle; support drops from the lower lip and the first audible sob leaks out on the exhale. In the latter part of the shot, tears travel down her cheeks, her head dips slightly, and the shoulders/back produce two uneven jolts. After the line, her mouth only opens and closes naturally for crying and breath; no extra words. Both hands stay in their table positions. She does not cover her face or wipe tears. Hold long enough to capture one post-break inhale. Cut away while the crying continues.

00:11.5–00:14, Shot 4, 85mm feel, Alin eye-level face close-up, locked, looking screen-right.
Lisa’s crying continues as a sound bridge. Alin’s jaw tightens briefly, her eyes wet up, and she lets out a small controlled exhale. Around 00:11.9–00:13.4 she quietly says, “I miss her too.” Let the tail of “too” tremble slightly. Then her gaze drops from Lisa’s face toward Lisa’s left hand on the table, and her right shoulder begins a small forward shift that initiates the reach with the right forearm. Her left hand stays on her thigh. Cut as the right forearm has already begun moving, so the next shot continues the same reach rather than restarting it.

00:14–00:16.5, Shot 5, fixed close overhead at roughly 45 degrees on the two hands, with a short section of both forearms included.
Alin’s right hand continues entering from frame left; Lisa’s left hand remains palm-down on frame right. Alin’s fingertips touch the back of Lisa’s hand first, then the palm settles gently over it and stays. Lisa’s fingers remain slightly curled at first, then relax a little after half a beat. No hand flip, no finger interlacing. This shot does only the contact: no stroking, no patting. Sound emphasizes a small fabric friction and the still-continuing sobbing. Cut after the contact has fully stabilized.

00:16.5–00:21, Shot 6, 65mm feel, level close shot focused on Alin, with Lisa’s soft out-of-focus side face and shoulder in the right foreground, locked.
After being touched, Lisa first lifts her eyes, then makes a small turn to find Alin. Alin waits until real eye contact exists before releasing tension in her jaw. Around 00:17.0–00:18.9 she says quietly, “We need to stay strong.” Let “we” include both of them; “strong” must not sound scolding. After a short beat, around 00:19.3–00:20.5 she says more softly, “Eat a little…” Her brow still carries slight tension, her eyes remain wet, and her gaze stays near Lisa’s eyes. Only after the line does she glance briefly down toward Lisa’s own plate, then back to Lisa. Their joined hands continue off-screen. Lisa’s shoulder slowly softens a little in the foreground under Alin’s calmer breathing, but she still has residual sobbing and does not give a mechanical nod. No extra gesture, no smile. Cut into the two-shot while preserving the same comfort moment.

00:21–00:25, Shot 7, 40mm feel, northwest-side two-shot medium, Alin left and Lisa right, with hands and the full table meal zone visible low in frame. A, B, and C are all visible again in their correct seat relationship, and the empty chair sits in the far middle-background.
Composition must prioritize keeping both A and B visible rather than blocked by forearms. For the first two seconds, the camera slides about 15 cm west while staying on the same axis side, so the forearms no longer overlap and the joined hands become clearly readable, then it locks off. Around 00:21.0–00:23.5 Alin continues, “We still have to get out—together.” Pause only briefly after “get out,” and let “together” land softly. Lisa keeps looking at Alin; when she hears “together,” she lets out one slightly longer exhale, though the residual crying remains. Around 00:23.5–00:25, Lisa lowers her eyes to her own plate, moves her right hand from beside the plate to the personal spoon, touches it, then grips the handle and holds it through the end. No extra pause and no second action. The spoon bowl stays against the plate edge, making only one light metal sound. She does not lift the spoon or eat. Alin’s right hand continues covering Lisa’s left hand, and her gaze follows the spoon-grip action. Her left hand remains on her thigh. Final live image: Lisa holding the spoon handle, tear tracks still visible, their other hands still joined, and the third meal still untouched. End naturally, no fade to black.

[Sound, Rhythm, and Continuity]
The soundtrack contains only the specified English dialogue, low room air through pipes, normal breathing, Lisa’s irregular sobbing, light metal contact on wood and tray, and small cloth friction. No extra dialogue, narration, lyrics, or background voices. Dialogue is the primary sound during the comfort passage; room tone and sobbing may soften slightly but never cut to silence. No music. Rhythm is driven by real breathing.
At the opening there is only the slight scrape of C being straightened; no scooping meat, pouring food, or serving-spoon contact with the can. Once Lisa breaks, the crying becomes the near-field sound focus, continuing through shots 4 and 5, then easing during the comfort passage without disappearing abruptly. Cloth sounds occur only when actual friction happens. Dust makes no sound.
Structure of rhythm:
first 4 seconds establish the three ready meals,
4–6 seconds suspend on the empty place,
6–11.5 seconds move from restraint into breakdown,
11.5–16.5 seconds turn through reaction and touch,
last 8.5 seconds settle through sustained eye contact, one longer exhale, and the spoon grip.
All movement is real-time. Do not use speed ramps, bullet time, shaky flash cuts, glow flares, or rotating camera tricks. Editing joins on action, eyeline, and the continuous crying bridge, never cutting away exactly when an expression starts to change. Color, tear tracks, clothing-fold structure, seats, and utensil states remain continuous. Off-screen bodies continue the same action state from the previous shot.

Priority order:
identity and spatial continuity > action/contact and emotional causality > readable eyes and true breathing > camera and physical detail.
Exclude face swaps, facial stretching, exaggerated mouth shapes, synchronized mechanical expressions, extra fingers or limbs, merged hands, drifting chairs, teleporting utensils, Alin’s meal appearing from nowhere, three meals collapsing into one, food suddenly appearing in an empty tray, ghost figures or reflected duplicates, subtitles, watermarks, or asset-board text. Always present one continuous lived moment of two adult women at the same table in the same room.

🎬 Long Cinematic AI Video Prompt

Prompt 

A cinematic teen drama short film, shot in warm golden-hour autumn light on the aluminum bleachers of a high school football stadium. The overall tone is naturalistic and emotionally intimate with a sudden comedic-revenge twist. Shallow depth of field, soft bokeh from sunlight hitting metal bleacher rails, handheld documentary-style camera with gentle drift, 24fps film grain, warm orange-and-teal color grade, lens flares from low sun.

**Shot 1 (0–5s):** Close-mid shot of a teenage girl with soft blonde hair pulled into a messy bun, wearing an off-shoulder cream sweater over a black tank top. She sits on metal bleachers scrolling intently on her phone. Beside her, a teenage boy in a light blue oversized hoodie with shaggy brown hair leans in close over her shoulder, peering at the screen with mild curiosity. Soft rim lighting from the setting sun behind them, blurred silver bleacher rows in the background, a few autumn leaves scattered on the seats.

**Shot 2 (5–9s):** Sudden jump cut — a burst of red smoke or colored powder explodes into frame, enveloping a small group of three teens sitting further down the bleachers. They flinch back in surprise, hands raised defensively to shield their faces, hair and loose strands whipped by the gust of the blast. Golden sunlight scatters through the red haze creating a hazy, dreamlike, slightly chaotic visual. Quick, reactive camera shake sells the surprise.

**Shot 3 (9–14s):** Intimate close-up portrait of a different girl — wavy, sunlit flyaway hair, delicate gold hoop earrings and a thin gold necklace, wearing a white knitted top. She looks down at her phone with a quiet, pensive, slightly worried expression, warm backlight haloing her hair, skin tones glowing in the low sun. The mood shifts from chaos to a quieter, tense beat.

**Shot 4 (14–20s):** Low-angle wide shot looking straight up at a bright yellow steel goalpost crossbar cutting diagonally across a clear, deep-blue late-afternoon sky. Below it, three teenagers stand on the field looking upward with concern and frustration — one boy in a grey hoodie with a black backpack reaches up and starts climbing the vertical post, straining to reach something lodged at the top. Two girls stand nearby, one with long brown hair looking up anxiously, the other in a navy striped sweater raising both hands toward the sky in a pleading/frustrated gesture. Their phones are visibly stuck on top of the crossbar. Blurred autumn-orange treeline and stadium floodlight tower visible at the edges of frame.

**Overall mood/theme:** "Messing with Amelia" backfires — a lighthearted teen revenge-prank narrative where the antagonist group's phones end up stranded on the stadium goalpost, and they're now desperately trying to climb up and fetch them. Comedic-ironic, youthful, slightly cinematic-trailer energy. Aspect ratio 1080x608, widescreen cinematic crop, subtle ambient wind/rustle sound design implied, no dialogue — purely visual storytelling with expressive reactions.

Seedance 2.5 prompt👇
Create a 25-second, 16:9, 11-shot realistic cinematic sequence in the same base shooting range, one continuous time span, with only two adult women: Alin and Lisa. No dialogue, no narration, no subtitles, no background voices.

Priority 1: Lisa begins already firing fast with obvious anger, not calm practice and not pure sadness: brows pulled inward and down, lower lids tight, jaw clenched, lips pressed thin, shoulders loaded, breath short and held. Priority 2: Alin remains completely off-screen until 05.5s, then enters and is fully set by 08.0s. Priority 3: after the handoff, Lisa must clearly hold one pistol in her right hand and the other in her left; both grips, both slides, both hands, and both forearms must remain visibly separate in character shots. Never make it look like both hands are on one gun.

Lisa is skilled and uses fast, heavy shooting to vent revenge-driven anger. Alin walks in from off-screen and gives Lisa the second pistol that had been tucked directly into Alin’s right-front waistband. Lisa takes it urgently, resists Alin’s gaze for a moment, then accepts it and resumes firing. The back half stays fast and dense; the change is internal: face shifts from clenched to loosened, motion from overforced to compact, breath from held to flowing. She ends still determined, never smiling or celebrating. All action stays real-time except the glass shatter at 20.0-21.6s, which is the only slow motion.

Reference binding:
Image 1 = Alin only: adult woman, pale blonde long straight hair with blunt bangs, white ruched camisole, blue jeans, brown belt, brown long boots, same facial structure and proportions.
Image 2 = Lisa only: adult woman, short blonde hair, orange-brown leather jacket with shearling collar, inner layer, deep brown waist cinch, short skirt, waist pouch, thigh strap, ankle boots; keep the real orange-brown color, never turn it red.
Image 3 = two identical black pistols only: same silhouette, metal finish, grip, and red-dot optic. Gun A starts in Lisa’s right hand. Gun B starts tucked directly into Alin’s right-front waistband above the beltline, no holster. Alin is off-screen at first, so gun B is also off-screen until she enters. The red-dot sight is not a laser emitter.
Image 4 = the base shooting range only: old concrete pillars, overhead pipes, warm hanging lamps, damp floor, yellow firing line, crates, rusted oil drums, bottle-and-can targets, steel plate and sandbag background, right-side corridor. Preserve the architectural depth. Exclude all board layout, labels, arrows, white background, and multi-view presentation.

Space and blocking:
Keep Image 4 layout. The target wall is north, the firing line south, the right corridor east. Lisa stands centered just south of the yellow line, facing north, and stays in the same foot zone the whole time. She can rotate slightly through the torso but never drifts sideways or walks toward the targets. Targets remain north.
Alin starts about 1.7 m southwest of Lisa, fully outside frame. Before 05.5s, no body part, reflection, or waist gun of Alin is visible. At 05.5s, after Lisa stops firing, Alin enters naturally from the rear-side frame edge, taking two normal steps along a short southwest-to-northeast path, moving about 1.1 m, then slowing to a stop about 0.6 m behind-left of Lisa. The camera must let the audience see the real entry and stop; never cut to an Alin already standing there. Gun B becomes visible only when she enters. After 08.0s both foot positions are fixed through the end. The handoff happens by natural arm reach only. Alin stays behind the firing line, never crosses Lisa’s arms, never moves to Lisa’s right side, never stands between muzzle and targets.
All human camera angles remain in the west half-space, so the shooting direction reads leftward in side views. Two-shots favor a southwest oblique angle so both faces are readable without blocking each other. Eye contact begins with the eyes, then a small head turn; torsos still face north. Guns stay lowered toward the target line during looks to the other person. In dual-gun shots, choose a shallow oblique angle that keeps the two guns visually separated; do not stack them into one silhouette or blur the far gun away.

Target continuity:
Two left cans are for the early hits. Midfield old bottle and can are for the later hits. The right green bottle is reserved only for the final hit. Target positions stay fixed. Damage accumulates: fallen cans remain down, broken bottle remnants and glass remain, and the green bottle stays intact until 20.0s. Debris never teleports to the women’s feet.

Gun-count proof, locked:
There are exactly two identical black pistols, tracked narratively as A and B, though no letters appear on screen.
00-08s: Lisa holds gun A in her right hand, left hand empty. Gun B is tucked in Alin’s right-front waistband, no holster, and remains off-screen with Alin until she enters.
08-11s: fixed medium two-shot from waist up. Lisa’s right-hand gun A is visible throughout. Alin draws gun B from her own waistband with her right hand and places it into Lisa’s empty left hand. Lisa stabilizes it, Alin releases and withdraws her now-empty hand. No tossing, flashing, or teleporting. The end of the shot must hold at least half a second proving the result: Lisa right hand = gun A, Lisa left hand = gun B, both hands and both guns separate and clear; Alin’s hands empty; Alin’s waistband empty.
11s-end: every character shot with Lisa must preserve two distinct pistols with visible spacing between hands. Both grips, both slides, and their corresponding forearms must be readable. During eye contact both guns stay low but still inside frame. When she resumes firing, each gun rises from its own hand. Lisa’s left hand always keeps gun B and never supports gun A. Gun A is never handed back, set down, or tucked away. Alin remains empty-handed after the transfer. If you cut to targets, off-screen continuity still preserves Lisa dual-wielding and Alin empty-handed. 13.0-16.6s must first show uninterrupted medium-shot dual-gun firing before any target insert. 17.3-20.0s must keep Lisa’s face and both guns in the same frame; no face-only close-up that hides the guns. 21.6-25.0s must also clearly show both guns in her hands.

Performance:
Lisa’s opening anger must read in the first second: inward-dropped brows, sharp eyes, tight lower lids, hard jawline, thin lips, loaded shoulders, held breath. This is emotional discharge, not neutral range practice. After the first burst she is still unsatisfied. The second burst is even more forceful. Even on hits her mouth stays tight. When Alin enters, Lisa only cuts her eyes first, then gives a short head turn; her body does not soften toward Alin. She takes the second gun briskly and wants to keep going immediately. Alin’s sustained gaze stops the lift for a beat. During the look, Lisa first keeps the jaw tight as if refusing to be seen, then glances away, returns to Alin, loosens the lips first, exhales longer, and only then lets the shoulders drop. This transition begins across the eye-contact beat and early second half, not instantly on contact. The first dual-gun burst still carries residue of her anger; after one short breath the jaw loosens further. She continues firing fast and dense, still focused and determined, but the mouth is no longer pressed thin and the shoulder reaction is more compact. She chooses when to stop; she is not interrupted by fear or collapse. At the end her eyes soften slightly toward Alin, then return to the targets with resolve. No smile, no sudden cheerfulness. The opening anger is absorbed into control, not erased.
Alin enters looking at the target zone, then quickly shifts to Lisa’s still-clenched face; this recognition slows her last step. Her brow tightens, jaw firms briefly, and her own pain is touched. She draws and offers the gun more steadily than Lisa moves, but without hesitation. When Lisa rushes to continue, Alin simply holds the gaze. Her lips part slightly and close again; finally she gives one exhale and a small shoulder drop. Only after Lisa begins to respond does Alin’s brow ease. During the second firing phase, Alin keeps watching seriously; only when she sees Lisa self-regulate does her slight forward lean relax. At the end she receives Lisa’s glance and gives one small nod.
Their reactions are staggered, never synchronized. Eyes lead, head follows. Keep subtle gaze shifts, natural blinks, and believable lamp reflections. Do not lock pupils or make both blink on every shot. Each shot carries only one dominant acting beat. No crying, no fresh tears, no spoken mouth shapes; lips only move with breathing. Face structure stays stable. In close shots, use smaller expression amplitude, but the difference between the tight opening face and the looser ending face must remain visible.

Rhythm and speed:
00-05.5s is rapid, weighty, continuous shooting. Do not turn it into evenly spaced shot-pause-shot timing. She is already in motion at frame one. Within a burst she does not lower the arm, check hits, or reset posture. Speed comes from short starts, chained reactions, and clean recoveries; gunshot pulses chase each other, and the next target reacts before the previous one finishes falling. The first shot contains one brief flourish between two firing bursts, but it is integrated into flow, not a pose. Real stop-fire begins only after 05.5s.

Los burritos deben verse algo más realistas que caricaturescos. Tono de parodia tierna, épica y levemente dramática. Sin diálogo. La narración se apoya en actuación, encuadre y timing cómico.
ENTORNO Y ATMÓSFERA
Paisaje inspirado en La Mancha: camino de tierra o sendero rural serpenteante, colinas suaves, terreno seco, pasto amarillento, tierra clara, piedras, horizonte amplio, aire castellano, luz natural. prompt:
Cinematic vertical sci-fi short, 36 seconds. A silver-haired man in a long black coat with ornate gold circular clockwork embroidery, with a small squirrel on his shoulder, travels through time inside a shimmering transparent bubble. The world around him jumps through eras: a burning, smoky primeval forest, a glowing sunset city seen from a hillside, an arctic ice field under a starry sky, a green wetland with mountains, and a pristine utopian city at golden hour. Cut to a short-cropped blonde woman in a sleek black dress watching a futuristic organic-architecture city, with white spiral towers and giant petal-shaped trees, flourish at sunrise. The man steps out of the bubble onto a glass walkway streaked with glowing orange and teal light lines, bursts through a sparkling energy explosion, and arrives in the future. A crowd of elegantly dressed people in muted earth tones, plus a woman in a pale silver gown, waits on the bridge. Warm golden-hour light, lens flares, shallow depth of field, soft atmospheric haze, epic yet calm mood, slow gliding camera, photoreal, high-end sci-fi film look, 9:16, 30fps.
Shot-by-shot version (better control):
Forest fire: Dark, smoky forest, embers glowing, slow drift forward. Time-lapse feel.
Woman on the balcony: Medium shot, blonde woman in a black dress raises a hand toward a futuristic city at golden hour. Birds fly across the sky, camera orbits slowly.
Bubble, sunset: Low-angle hero shot of the man in the clockwork coat inside a glass bubble, with a city of lights glowing behind him.
Light bridge: Woman stands on a reflective walkway with streaking orange and teal light lines, giant petal-trees behind her.
Bubble, ice age: Man looks up at the starry sky on an ice field, bubble shimmering.
Bubble, wetlands: Rear shot of the man looking over green wetlands and mountains, squirrel on his shoulder.
Bubble, haze: Soft pastel haze, the bubble starts to dissolve.
Bubble, utopia: The bubble lands on a glass bridge, with a utopian skyline and spheres on towers behind him.
Burst: The man sprints forward through an explosion of golden sparks and light streaks, the bubble bursting around him.
Arrival: He slows to a walk and meets the waiting crowd, then the woman in the pale gown steps forward, the camera pushing in gently.

SCENE AND GEOGRAPHY
Inside the referenced abandoned pumping station, the enormous pump wheel stands beneath the rear arched window. Canal railing stays left, furnace and staircase stay right. Keep the existing architecture recognizable.

The woman stands screen-left at a waist-high brass control socket attached to the pump housing. The man stands screen-right, one step behind her, holding down a stiff mechanical safety lever with his RIGHT hand. Both faces are visible in the first frame. Her left forearm instrument is already aligned with the socket; her right hand supports its casing.

They are trying to restart the station together. She needs his trust; he needs her to finish without getting hurt.

FOUR SHOTS — EXACTLY 10 SECONDS
Hard cuts at 2.2, 4.3 and 7.0 seconds. One clear camera movement per shot. Maintain the woman-left / man-right screen relationship and stay on the same side of their interaction axis.

SHOT 1 — 0.0–2.2s
Low, wide two-shot, seen just above a shallow foreground puddle. Both characters and the dormant wheel are readable immediately. A short lateral camera slide clears a foreground pipe, revealing their full working relationship.

The woman presses her left forearm instrument into the socket. Before committing, she checks the man's face to see whether he will keep holding the lever. He meets her look and deliberately braces his weight against it. She turns her attention back to the connection. A thin cyan seam lights inside the socket.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 2 — 2.2–4.3s
Intimate medium close-up from beside the pump housing: her face dominates the left foreground, his face remains readable behind her on the right. A restrained forward push closes the distance.

Cyan light climbs from the connected instrument onto her cheek. She watches the mechanism for a response, then checks him again, seeking acknowledgment that it worked. His attention moves past her toward a vibrating pressure coupling beside the wheel. His grip tightens on the safety lever. The mechanical hum becomes uneven; a bolt rattles visibly in its seat.

HARD CUT ON THE METALLIC SNAP.

SHOT 3 — 4.3–7.0s
Low, wide side view with both full bodies visible from the first frame. A fast, short backward tracking move makes room for their retreat.

The coupling vents a single forceful jet of white steam above shoulder height, aimed toward the empty foreground, not into either face. The woman recoils one step, disengaging her forearm instrument from the socket. The man releases the lever and catches her RIGHT upper arm with his LEFT hand, guiding her behind his shoulder as he takes one grounded step back.

Their boots displace shallow water. Her jacket hem and his long coat respond to the pressure with delayed fabric movement. The heavy pump wheel begins turning behind them. The danger is brief and physically localized, not an explosion that destroys the room.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 4 — 7.0–10.0s
Medium-wide two-shot from the same side of the action axis. The woman remains left and the man right; the rear arch and distant city are visible between and above them. A smooth backward dolly widens the composition.

He releases her arm once she has her footing. She briefly meets his eyes, checking whether he still trusts her. Before either can settle, a deep mechanical pulse sounds beyond the station. He notices the distant response first; she follows his gaze a fraction later.

Beyond the arch, three successive clusters of amber windows switch on across the previously dark city, traveling away into the distance. Their successful repair has awakened a larger connected system. Both turn toward it, their partnership now facing a new question.

Woman: win his continued cooperation by making the machine respond. Her obstacle is that the machinery becomes dangerous just as she proves her point. Pursue his trust through purposeful checks of his face; after the rescue, assess his response instead of celebrating or posing.

Man: give her the chance to succeed while keeping her within reach. His obstacle is that protecting her may require interrupting the experiment. First support her by holding the lever; then redirect her physically out of danger. Afterward, check her footing before investigating the distant sound.

Keep attention engaged with the partner or the active mechanism. Natural blinks, responsive breathing, no fixed smiles, synchronized reactions or blank heroic stares.

Bodies retain weight and traction. The man guides rather than throws her. Machinery accelerates with inertia. Steam disperses and wet footprints persist across cuts. Painted highlights and moving shadows follow the same stable character forms.

prompt:
30 seconds, 16:9, cinematic animation with realistic adult human proportions and real materials, normal-speed motion, natural motion blur. One continuous nighttime campfire dinner scene told in 8 cuts. Three adult women talk about life after leaving the dead city. A small detection drone performs routine patrol and shoots down one harassing crow. The guard incident must not interrupt the conversation rhythm: at most a casual glance, no panic, no standing in alarm, no sword-grabbing, no stopping the fish roast. Outside the fence is harsh and dangerous; by the fire, they can still read each other’s eyes and smiles. All intelligible dialogue must use only the English lines listed below. No subtitles, narration, opening or ending cards.

[Reference Responsibilities]
Image 1 = Alin, wounded platinum-haired adult woman. Lock face shape, light eyes, blunt bangs, torn white top, blue jeans, boots, and scar positions. Add one weathered gray-brown blanket over her legs without changing the clothing. She remains weak from severe injury and stays seated and supported throughout.
Image 2 = Lisa, short blonde adult woman. Lock face shape, blue eyes, orange-brown leather jacket with pale fur collar, inner layers, dark skirt, waist bag, and ankle boots. Never rename her Elin.
Image 3 = Hia, dark-haired adult woman with a bun. Lock East Asian face, hair ornament, dark blue-black and deep red embroidered long coat, belt, and boots. Her sheathed long sword stays on the outer side of her bench for the whole scene; never rename her Jia.
Image 4 = the only environment reference. Keep the spatial relationship among shipping container, canopy, corrugated fence, gate, fire pit, benches, water jar, and worktable; convert daytime to deep night. Use the main wide view to set layout; the fire-pit detail view only informs materials and structure. Render as one complete location. Do not include reference layouts, labels, numbers, split panels, or character turnarounds.
Image 5 = the only detection drone: orange-yellow spherical shell, central observation eye, two side-deploying firing units. Keep the reference structure. It shoots short pulse lasers; the center eye observes, the laser emits from the side barrels.
Image 6 = bloodthirsty crow reference for feathers, beak, claws, and dark red eyes. Keep normal real crow size and avian skeletal structure. Eyes only catch dim reflections and do not glow outward.

Only three humans appear: Alin, Lisa, Hia, plus one drone. Character identity, costume, prop design, and material finish come only from their own references and cannot be swapped.

[Real Scale]
All three women follow normal adult female scale, roughly 1.65–1.75 m standing height. Perspective may change screen size but not world scale.
Crows are normal-sized: about 40–45 cm beak to tail, 80–90 cm wingspan, never giant ravens or raptors.
The drone is small: folded sphere about 12 cm diameter, about 20 cm wide when firing units are deployed, small enough to hold in one hand, smaller than an adult head and clearly smaller than a same-depth crow torso. It hovers about 2.2–2.6 m above ground. Never stage it as a large UAV or manned craft. Keep fence posts, canopy edges, or crows in frame as scale references, and avoid ultra-close wide-angle enlargement.
There are only three fish, each about 25 cm long, skewered on thin branches about 60 cm long, with visible tail fins and blistered skin.
The stone-ring fire pit is about 1.2 m wide. The burning zone stays modest: mostly glowing coals with flames about 20–35 cm high. Fish roast over the coal edge nearest the characters, not in the center of the flames.

[Locked Space and Blocking]
Use the main viewing direction from the gate side toward the rear container as the scene axis, called south-to-north for this scene only. Fire pit center is the origin. Screen right is east; the container side is north.

A = Alin = Image 1. Fixed north of the fire, slightly west, around (-0.35, 1.65)m. She leans against a wooden crate with an old cushion, body turned south-southeast so she can see the other two. Her head and shoulders must always remain visible between them and never be fully blocked by furniture or bodies.
B = Lisa = Image 2. Starts seated on the north end of the northwest bench, around (-0.95, 0.45)m, body facing southeast, able to turn toward Hia. She is about 1.3 m from Alin, feet planted on clear ground outside the fire ring.
C = Hia = Image 3. Fixed on the northeast bench, around (0.95, 0.45)m, body facing southwest toward Lisa. Both feet stay grounded. She never changes seats or stands.

Before 18 seconds, all three stay fixed at their ground positions. From 18–21 seconds, Lisa takes the largest fish, rises from the north end of her bench, walks two small steps along the west side of the fire to crouch beside Alin at about (-0.90, 1.55)m, with shoulders roughly 0.55 m apart. She always avoids the stone ring and Hia, never crosses the fire, never passes through furniture, never teleports. After 21 seconds she stays there until the end.

All camera angles remain in the southern fan of this triangle. Lisa always stays on world west, Hia on world east, Alin on world north. Close-ups may reframe but must not swap positions. Camera can move; the floor anchors do not. Lisa is the only character with one clear relocation.

At the start, all three fish are set into the north half of the fire’s coal edge. The largest one is in front of Lisa’s right hand; Lisa tends it, then later removes it with her right hand and offers it to Alin. One fish remains in its original place. The third is in front of Hia. From 27–30 seconds Hia removes the one in front of her. Final fish state: Alin and Lisa jointly support the largest fish, Hia holds one fish, and one fish remains by the fire. Total remains three.

The drone follows a slow closed patrol route above the fence, autonomously adjusting orientation. It continues patrolling off-screen as well and stabilizes only briefly at the kill moment. Around 12 seconds it reaches the east inner fence line and fires outward, away from people and food. Three crows begin in fixed zones: one on the east canopy edge, one on the west fence top, one outside the south gate wall. Only the east crow is shot down. The other two remain in their original zones with only minor head turns, wing tucks, or foot shifts, never becoming a sudden flock.

[Unified Tone and Five-Color Palette]
Overall look: low-saturation cold gray-blue post-apocalyptic night, with localized amber campfire warmth. Preserve natural skin tone, rough metal, leather, and dust texture. HEX values are art references only, never on screen.
Midnight blue-black #151E28: sky and deepest ruins beyond the fence, dark but still readable.
Cool steel gray-blue #526373: moonlit metal, canopy roof, and background shadow.
Weathered wood gray-brown #766457: benches, dirt, blanket, and unlit daily objects.
Ember amber #D9954E: near-fire highlights, fish skin reflections, warm cloth edges, restricted to the fire zone.
Natural warm skin #C89E87: skin under firelight, with each woman retaining her own reference complexion; Alin slightly pale but never blue.

Campfire gives a local 2000–2400K warmth. Night ambience feels like weak 6500–7500K skylight. Camera white balance stays fixed around 4300K across all shots. Background is about two stops darker than faces, but shadow sides of faces still hold eyes, scars, and costume layers. Protect Alin’s white shirt and platinum hair from turning orange. Keep Lisa’s jacket orange-brown, not fluorescent orange. Hia’s dark coat must still show folds and embroidery.
The fire is the only warm world light source. The side facing the fire reads warmer; the opposite side keeps a slight cold edge. When camera angle changes, light direction changes according to space only; never invent frontal beauty light. Highlights roll off softly, fire reflections in eyes stay small and flicker subtly, and skin retains texture. Keep one consistent black level, shadow hue, and fine grain. No heavy teal-orange grade, no full-frame yellow haze, no fake day-for-night.

[Performance and Fixed Voices]
Lisa wants Hia to catch her joke about opening a shop, then bring Alin into it. She talks while minding the fish, eyes lifting before the head. When Hia reminds her, she turns the fish and briefly presses her lips; she never plays cute to camera. When Alin joins in, Lisa looks to her first and then lets the smile open. When handing over the fish, she slows down and protects Alin’s weak grip. Natural blinking, small gaze shifts, firelight in the eyes. Body rhythm alternates between light and careful, never constant bouncing, never broad laughter.
Lisa Voice: "An adult woman with a light, clear mid-range voice and a neutral conversational English accent. Brisk but unhurried phrasing, playful emphasis, a soft smile in the voice; gentler volume when addressing Alin."

Hia lets Lisa keep fantasizing while still tending food. Neck and shoulders loose but stable, hand movements economical, gaze moving with purpose among fish, Lisa, and Alin. Slow natural blinks. On her first line, she looks at the fish before lifting her eyes and teases in a short sentence. The patrol shot only earns one casual checking glance; breath and hand rhythm never break. At the end she looks at Lisa, lifts the corner of her mouth slightly, and accepts the promise without playing sadness or farewell.
Hia Voice: "An adult woman with a low, clear, lightly textured voice and a neutral conversational English accent. Economical phrasing, steady breath, dry understated humor; soft volume and clean consonants."

Alin wants to join the joke but still needs physical support. Her back and shoulders stay against the cushion, breathing shallow but continuous, arm movements small. When Lisa talks about the shop, Alin’s eyes follow Lisa first, then she answers with a little smile. She takes a light inhale before speaking; voice is soft but clear, no coughing, no sudden upright recovery, no return to strength. When receiving the fish, she only lifts the nearer left hand and Lisa helps support it. Her smile lives in the eyes and mouth corners, never a big laugh.
Alin Voice: "An adult woman with a soft, slightly breathy mid-low voice and a neutral conversational English accent. Quiet, gently spaced words on limited breath, with understated dry humor; never whispery to the point of losing clarity."

In close shots, keep moist eyes, small gaze shifts, and natural blinking. Listeners may begin to lift their eyes or smile before the speaker fully finishes, but must not interrupt. Only the current speaker performs English mouth shapes; others only breathe or smile. The five dialogue lines are each spoken once only, with stable voice character across cuts and no added shouting, exposition, or improvised lines.

[Wind, Fire, Dust, and Guard Effects]
A light breeze stays fixed from west to east, left-to-right in the main view. Character performance remains the primary foreground action; environmental effects stay low-intensity and never all compete as visual centers.

Fire: thin wood and red coals burn steadily. Flames rise first, then drift slightly east. A few sparks rise on heat, float a few dozen centimeters, then dim out; no full-screen particles. Thin smoke rises from the fuel and drifts east, away from faces and mouths. Small oil drops from fish skin may hit coals with a soft sizzle but never repeated flare-ups. Heat distortion exists only in a small area above the fire; faces stay stable and readable.

Breeze: Lisa’s short hair tips move lightly; the fur collar only trembles slightly. Hia’s bun stays intact; fine hairs and ribbon ends occasionally drift east; coat hem lifts a little and settles. Alin’s hair edges move gently; the blanket corner trembles while the part resting on her legs stays weighted. Heavy leather only folds with body movement and never flutters like silk. Loose canopy edges tremble lightly, corrugated metal may click softly, and dust stays sparse and low enough that facial features remain readable.

Shooting: the drone stabilizes, makes one short aiming adjustment, shows a tiny glow at the side barrel, then fires one narrow short warm-white laser directly to the target. No projectile, no sustained barrage, no thick beam, no full-screen flash. The beam is only faintly visible in thin dust and does not alter exposure. The impact on the crow creates only a small hot point and two or three loose feathers, with no fireball or blood mist.

Crow action: after pushing off from the canopy edge, the wings beat with realistic avian mechanics and flexible primary feathers. After impact it loses lift and drops along its existing outward trajectory. Wings and tail change position during the fall; the body never freezes stiff in air. It lands on dry sand outside the east wall, creating one small low dust puff that drifts east and settles. The fall stays far from the dinner; no feathers or body parts fly near the food. The drone then retracts its firing posture and resumes patrol. The other crows’ head turns and foot shifts do not sync with the humans.

[English Dialogue and Timing]
